title: Add design note explaining position 0 for implicit @everyone role
description:
The spec hardcodes 'position 0' as the slot for the implicit @everyone role at draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md:560: 'The implicit @everyone role (position 0) is held by all Space members and is not included in the roles array.'

The choice of position 0 is intentional and architecturally significant — it anchors @everyone as the lowest-priority role in the position-ordered hierarchy. If position semantics ever change (descending → ascending order, integer → fractional positions, or repurposing position 0 for something else), the implicit @everyone slot becomes a special-case carve-out that needs to be remembered.

Currently there is no explanatory comment in the spec describing why position 0 specifically. The information lives only in the one declarative sentence at line 560.

Suggested fix: add a brief design note alongside the SpaceRole.position field definition, or in §Space Permission Resolution, explicitly stating:
- Position values are unsigned integers, sorted descending (higher = outranks lower)
- Position 0 is reserved for the implicit @everyone role
- Defined SpaceRoles MUST have position > 0
- This means @everyone is always the lowest-priority role; this is intentional

This is a minor doc-only addition. Not blocking anything; just hardens a design choice against future drift.

Identified during the 2026-05-12 session's principal-name survey.
acceptance_criteria:
- A brief design note appears either at SpaceRole.position field definition or in §Space Permission Resolution
- The note covers: position is unsigned int sorted descending; position 0 is reserved for @everyone; defined roles MUST have position > 0
- The wording is minimal (one to three sentences) — this is hardening a design choice, not introducing new behavior
